title: Arabic MSA — Free Intensive Foundation to Independent Bridge

target.few_month_goal: Complete a strong beginner-to-independent MSA foundation, roughly strong A2 / early B1 if checkpoints are passed.
target.long_term_goal: Continue from the same system toward B2, C1 and C2; do not label the learner C2 based on time or playlist completion.
target.reality_note: Arabic C2 is not a credible few-month promise. Advancement is checkpoint-based.

blocks: 20–30 min grammar clinic on selected days

source_roles.anu_marhaba: Primary curriculum spine: 23 MSA lessons, four skills, multimedia EPUB.
source_roles.wisconsin: Audio-first and alternate-speaker reinforcement; introductions, greetings, pronunciation, travel and targeted listening.
source_roles.msu_i: Semester-1 structured practice: vocabulary, grammar, reading, writing, embedded audio. Use Standard-Arabic sections; tag/skip Egyptian-only sections in the MSA core.
source_roles.msu_ii: Semester-2 structured A2-building practice with audio, quizzes, writing and speaking. Use Standard-Arabic sections; Egyptian modules remain optional/dialect-tagged.
source_roles.madinah_lq: Parallel grammar-depth clinic with English audio; 2–3 sessions weekly, not the communicative spine.
source_roles.dli_gloss: Later transfer source for graded MSA listening/reading once beginner material is stable.

completed_prior_milestones: singular, dual and plural address basics

phases.name: Foundation and self-introduction
phases.anu: Marhaba lessons 1–5; move quickly through material already mastered.
wisconsin: Arabic Intro Lesson: Greetings in MSA
Common Greetings in Arabic — delayed review
msu: Elementary Arabic I: selected Unit I review
phases.checkpoint: A1-start: understand and produce a short greeting/introduction exchange without English prompts.

phases.name: Core sentence system
msu: Elementary Arabic I 3.2 present tense with food vocabulary
phases.checkpoint: Build new nominal and simple verbal sentences rather than reciting memorized phrases.

phases.name: Finish introductory MSA
phases.reinforcement: Wisconsin old-topic retrieval after 5–12 item gaps; no same-topic back-to-back review.
phases.checkpoint: A1 exit / A2 entry: routine personal information, basic description, present-tense statements/questions, usable reading of short MSA text.

phases.name: A2 expansion
phases.anu: Marhaba lessons 18–23; complete the full Marhaba course.
msu: Elementary Arabic II Units I–III: Standard-Arabic vocabulary/grammar/reading/writing
skip or separately tag Egyptian-only speaking sections
phases.madinah_lq: Book 1 lessons 18–23; finish Book 1 grammar clinic
phases.dli_gloss: Begin easy Arabic-MSA Level 1/1+ listening/reading items, 2 per week.
phases.checkpoint: A2 core: understand the main point of clear familiar MSA, describe self/family/study, and write connected short paragraphs.

phases.name: Independent-language bridge
msu: Elementary Arabic II Units IV–VIII, prioritizing Standard-Arabic vocabulary/grammar/reading/writing
phases.dli_gloss: Arabic-MSA Level 1+ then selected Level 2 items as comprehension allows, 3–4 items/week.
phases.madinah_lq: Begin Book 2 selectively for grammar gaps only; do not let grammar replace listening/output.
outputs: oral summary of a short recording
phases.checkpoint: Strong A2 / early-B1 bridge if the learner can understand clear standard speech on familiar subjects and produce connected MSA without heavy scripting.

spaced_media_rule.rolling_ratio: roughly 70% new / 30% reinforcement early, moving toward 60/40

actions: keep Arabic-script-only card fronts and eight-layer backs
otherwise advance to next free active-course media
